newsitem.title: USA: Court lets Orange County suit proceed - report.
newsitem.headline: Court lets Orange County suit proceed - report.

text.p: A federal judge has ruled that Orange County, Calif., can proceed with its bankruptcy-related lawsuit against the federal government's Office of Finance, according to a published report Thursday.

U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor in Santa Ana ruled that the county could press ahead with the lawsuit, which named the United States and the Office of Finance as defendants along with the Federal Home Loan Banks, according to the Los Angeles Times Orange County edition.
Earlier this week, U.S. Department of Justice lawyers urged Taylor to dismiss the lawsuit. But the judge said he could find "no immunity as a matter of law," the Times said.
The Federal Home Loan Bank System supplies credit reserves for savings and loans, cooperative banks and other mortgage lenders. It is made up of 12 Federal Home Loan Banks.
The county sued the Office of Finance last year, alleging it acted on behalf of the Federal Home Loan Banks in transactions involving risky securities.
Orange County attorney Michael Swartz said the ruling clears the way for the case to proceed toward trial.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection in December 1994 after sustaining losses estimated at more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
